title: Private hire car driver numbers and whether they will be managed
asked: Mr Vikram Nair asked whether the steady increase in Private Hire Car Driver's Vocational Licences is a sustainable trend, and whether there are plans to manage the number of private hire car drivers.
response: The number of PHC Driver's Vocational Licences has been roughly maintained at the same level for the past few years, and there are no plans to constrain the total number of drivers. PHCs are an important mode of transport for people who cannot or do not want to own a car but want pay-per-use private transport. The point-to-point population has grown from 28,000 ten years ago to about 70,000 today, with about 400,000 rides a day, complementing public transport. The Minister said the number has stabilised and there is no intention to curtail it.

key_points.point: The number of PHC Driver's Vocational Licences has been roughly maintained at the same level for the past few years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The number of PHC Driver’s Vocational Licences has continued to be roughly maintained at the same level for the past few years.

key_points.point: There are no plans at the moment to constrain the total number of drivers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: There are no plans at the moment for us to constrain the total number of drivers.

key_points.point: PHCs provide for people who are unable to drive or unwilling to own a car but want access to private transport on a pay-per-use basis.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: they provide for people who are unable to drive or are unwilling to own a car but yet would like to have access to private transport on a pay-per-use basis

key_points.point: The point-to-point population has increased from 28,000 ten years ago to roughly 70,000 today.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: The taxi or the point-to-point population has increased from 28,000 10 years ago, to roughly around 70,000 today.

key_points.point: Total rides are about 400,000 a day, complementing public transport provision.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: it is about 400,000 a day, that is substantial and it complements our public transport provision

key_points.point: There is no intention to curtail the number, and the number has stabilised over time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: we have no intention at the moment to curtail the number, but I think the number has stabilised over time.

key_points.point: PHC drivers are a diverse group, including professional full-time drivers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: There are professional drivers who are doing the same thing as taxi drivers, driving full-time.

key_points.point: Some PHC drivers are in transient employment and use driving to earn income between jobs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: There are people who are also in transient employment and this is a good way for them to come in and continue to earn an income, maybe when they are in between jobs.

key_points.point: The Minister would appreciate if some PHC drivers go into the bus industry to help address the public bus constraint.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: Certainly, I would appreciate if some of them go into the bus industry, help us address the constraint that we have for public buses.

key_points.point: The decision on numbers is left to the market.
key_points.speaker: Mr Jeffrey Siow
key_points.quote: But we have to leave it to the market and to let them decide.

supplementary: Whether the market should be left alone or intervened in if PHC driver numbers grow too large or incomes fall.
